issue_context.title: Remove or parameterize google.com from test cases
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

We added pinging google.com to the original E2Es, however in airgapped environments, these tests fail for obvious reasons:

```
Get http://google.com: dial tcp: lookup google.com on 192.48.0.10:53: server misbehaving
```

- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/windows/hybrid_network.go 
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/network/networking.go
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/network/dns.go

In general, we need to parameterize this if possible.



### What did you expect to happen?

Running the `sig-network` or `sig-windows` tests should pass in air-gapped environments, especially those that dont explicitly declare external connectivity.  
For example:

```

[sig-network] Networking Granular Checks: Services 
  should function for client IP based session affinity: udp [LinuxOnly]
  /workspace/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/network/networking.go:283
[BeforeEach] [sig-network] Networking
  /workspace/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/framework.go:178
STEP: Creating a kubernetes client
Dec 15 06:29:14.990: INFO: >>> kubeConfig: /tmp/kubeconfig-609614051
STEP: Building a namespace api object, basename nettest
STEP: Binding the e2e-test-privileged-psp PodSecurityPolicy to the default service account in nettest-7422
STEP: Waiting for a default service account to be provisioned in namespace
[BeforeEach] [sig-network] Networking
  /workspace/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/network/networking.go:94
STEP: Executing a successful http request from the external internet
Dec 15 06:29:19.125: FAIL: Unable to connect/talk to the internet: Get http://google.com: dial tcp: lookup google.com on 192.48.0.10:53: server misbehaving
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run the `sig-network` test suites inside of a kuberentes cluster which has no internet connection.

```
sonobuoy run --e2e-focus=“sig-network” --e2e-skip="Distruptive|Slow|ExternalLoadBalancer"
```

review_comments: Hmm, I'm not sure why we had ``assertConsistentConnectivity`` from the Linux container to ``8.8.8.8`` before, but I think it would make more sense to have it from the Windows container to ``8.8.8.8`` instead, since this is ``test/e2e/windows`` after all.

@claudiubelu as it is mentioned [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/windows/hybrid_network.go#L52) that here we are checking internet connectivity for both Windows and Linux pods that's why have `assertConsistentConnectivity from the Linux container to 8.8.8.8`. Please correct me if I am wrong here. And also thanks for your input.
I was confused at the beginning too, but seems this whole test block is for hybrid, not windows only

> @claudiubelu as it is mentioned [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/windows/hybrid_network.go#L52) that here we are checking internet connectivity for both Windows and Linux pods that's why have `assertConsistentConnectivity from the Linux container to 8.8.8.8`. Please correct me if I am wrong here. And also thanks for your input.

Right, but in that case, it was testing Linux -> Internet (8.8.8.8), Windows -> Internet (google.com), and after that Linux -> Windows, and then Windows -> Linux. After all, I think it made sense in that scenario; it was a good idea to make sure both Linux and Windows network connections were properly set up before testing the Linux - Windows connection. If you'd test the Linux - Windows connection directly and it'd fail, you wouldn't know who's fault it is.

Looking back in history, the most important part is testing out the Linux -> Windows and Windows -> Linux connectivity (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74377), the other checks were made to ensure networking works in both pods in the first place. I don't think that connecting to 8.8.8.8 or google.com specifically is relevant for the test, IMO. I think connecting to the Kubernetes API instead should be sufficient. @jayunit100 , what do you think?

> , it was testing Linux -> Internet (8.8.8.8), Windows -> Internet (google.com), and after that Linux -> Windows, and then Windows -> Linux. After all, I think it made sense in that scenario; it was a good idea to make sure both Linux and Windows network connections were properly set up before testing the Linux - Windows connection.

> the other checks were made to ensure networking works in both pods in the first place

internet connectivity from pods doesn't guarantee that intra-pod communication works, internet connectivity should be a separate test case that can be filtered,  this is why the bug was opened, doesn't it?

right, we want to test both of these things. In some contexts it makes sense not to expect internet connectivity, but it is a useful check to see that we didn't royally break something in say, kube-proxy :-)

putting external network connectivity in a separate tagged test will allow excluding them in environments where the test failing is working as intended
